atoms.b: In Roman times, women had much ((++fewer more)) rights and job opportunities than men. They could not vote, hold political office or join the army.
Some Roman women could own small businesses or property, but their main ((++responsibilities hobbies)) were raising children and taking care of the household.

atoms.text: Roman society was strongly divided by social class. Enslaved people carried out most household work for wealthy families. This meant upper-class women were often relieved of responsibilities that poorer women had to handle themselves.

Children’s lives also depended on class. Wealthy boys could go to school and learn reading and writing, but poor boys often had to work instead of studying. Girls were rarely educated, no matter their class, as they were mostly expected to marry young.
